- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts too high; cap forecast at 2–3% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with sentiment moderation.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 70, forecast often drops too aggressively; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to avoid premature correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates late-period price increases (especially >70) when sentiment is positive; add 0.5–2% tail-up bias for final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead in direction of sentiment momentum.
